titleText.es: Dentro de 60 millones de años, los extraterrestres conocerán a los humanos solo por un vídeo borroso de una mujer en un anuncio de Axe.
titleText.en: In sixty million years aliens will know humans only by a fuzzy clip of a woman in an Axe commercial.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official English title attributes are preserved exactly. OCR interleaved simultaneous panel text, omitted accents, fused true line wraps, misread CUANDO/EL/MUCHO, and produced one false flower-art token; the authored order follows the visible conversation. Ophrys apifera is audited as one excluded Latin scientific name with two physical boxes.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Orquídeas is the plural of orquídea.

example.es: Las orquídeas florecen en primavera.
example.en: The orchids bloom in spring.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cuyas links a feminine plural possession to the person or thing mentioned before it. It agrees with the possessed noun, not the owner.

example.es: Conocí a una autora cuyas novelas admiro.
example.en: I met an author whose novels I admire.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Flores is the plural of flor.

example.es: El jardín tiene flores amarillas.
example.en: The garden has yellow flowers.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Parecen is the plural present form of parecer. Before a noun it can describe resemblance, without saying that the things are literally identical.

example.es: Esas nubes parecen montañas.
example.en: Those clouds look like mountains.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Abejas is the plural of abeja.

example.es: Las abejas visitan las flores.
example.en: The bees visit the flowers.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: For an animal, hembra identifies the female sex. It can follow the species noun and does not change for number in the same way as an ordinary adjective.

example.es: Vimos dos lobos hembra.
example.en: We saw two female wolves.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Machos is the plural noun for male animals.

example.es: Los machos tienen plumaje oscuro.
example.en: The males have dark plumage.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a noun for an animal, macho means a male.

example.es: Ningún macho se acercó.
example.en: No male came near.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Intentan is the present form of intentar for a plural subject.

example.es: Intentan resolver el problema.
example.en: They try to solve the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aparearse is a pronominal verb used for animals mating. Its small pronoun changes with the subject.

example.es: Las aves vuelven para aparearse.
example.en: The birds return to mate.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ellas is the feminine plural stressed pronoun. After a preposition it can mean ‘them.’

example.es: Hablé con ellas ayer.
example.en: I spoke with them yesterday.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Transfieren is the plural present form of transferir.

example.es: Las tuberías transfieren el calor.
example.en: The pipes transfer the heat.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the small pronoun used with posarse
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Posarse is used when something lands or settles on a surface. The small pronoun changes with the subject: me poso, se posa, se posan.

example.es: La mariposa se posa en una hoja.
example.en: The butterfly lands on a leaf.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With se, posa is the singular present form of posarse, used when an animal or object comes to rest on a surface.

example.es: El pájaro se posa en la rama.
example.en: The bird lands on the branch.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mimetiza is the singular present form of mimetizar.

example.es: El insecto mimetiza una hoja seca.
example.en: The insect mimics a dry leaf.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the small pronoun used with extinguirse
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Extinguirse describes a species, fire, or activity dying out. The small pronoun is part of this use.

example.es: La especie se extinguió hace siglos.
example.en: The species died out centuries ago.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With se, extinguió is a completed-past form of extinguirse for one species or thing.

example.es: Ese animal se extinguió hace mucho.
example.en: That animal became extinct long ago.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Compañeras can mean companions or partners. For animals in a reproductive context, it can refer to mates.

example.es: Los pájaros buscan a sus compañeras.
example.en: The birds look for their mates.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recurren is the plural present form of recurrir. With a it describes turning to a measure or solution.

example.es: A veces recurren a métodos antiguos.
example.en: Sometimes they resort to old methods.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recurrir requires a before the measure, method, or person turned to.

example.es: Recurrió a una solución temporal.
example.en: She resorted to a temporary solution.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Autopolinización is pollination using pollen from the same flower or plant.

example.es: La planta puede reproducirse por autopolinización.
example.en: The plant can reproduce by self-pollination.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Genética is the feminine singular adjective related to genes or heredity.

example.es: Estudian la diversidad genética.
example.en: They study genetic diversity.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recurso can be something available for solving a problem, including a last resort.

example.es: La negociación fue nuestro último recurso.
example.en: Negotiation was our last resort.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Retrasa is the singular present form of retrasar.

example.es: La lluvia retrasa la salida.
example.en: The rain delays the departure.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Inevitable has the same form with masculine and feminine singular nouns.

example.es: El cambio parece inevitable.
example.en: The change seems inevitable.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Existió is a completed-past form of existir for one person or thing.

example.es: Ese puente existió durante siglos.
example.en: That bridge existed for centuries.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por can introduce the evidence or clue that lets someone know or recognize something.

example.es: Lo reconocí por la voz.
example.en: I recognized him from his voice.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aspecto can describe what someone or something looks like.

example.es: El edificio tiene un aspecto antiguo.
example.en: The building has an old appearance.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: in; from (as part of a ojos de)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This a begins the fixed expression a ojos de, which introduces a person's or group's perspective.

example.es: A ojos del jurado, la prueba era clara.
example.en: In the jury's eyes, the evidence was clear.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Interpretada is the feminine singular completed-action form of interpretar.

example.es: La señal fue interpretada por el equipo.
example.en: The signal was interpreted by the team.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is the living-organism sense of planta, not a floor of a building or an industrial facility.

example.es: La planta necesita luz.
example.en: The plant needs light.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This sense names an artistic picture made with paint, not the paint material itself.

example.es: El museo compró una pintura antigua.
example.en: The museum bought an old painting.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dibujada is the feminine singular completed-action form of dibujar used as a description.

example.es: Vimos una figura dibujada a mano.
example.en: We saw a figure drawn by hand.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Moribunda is the feminine singular form used for a living being near death.

example.es: Intentaron salvar la planta moribunda.
example.en: They tried to save the dying plant.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Recordaré is the simple future form of recordar for yo.

example.es: Recordaré tu consejo.
example.en: I will remember your advice.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How does Spanish say ‘whose’ while matching the thing possessed?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use cuyo, cuya, cuyos, or cuyas before the possessed noun; match that noun in gender and number.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form agrees with what is possessed, not with the owner. Cuyas ideas means ‘whose ideas’ because ideas is feminine plural.

example.es: Conozco a un músico cuyas canciones son famosas.
example.en: I know a musician whose songs are famous.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something resembles or looks like a kind of thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of parecer followed directly by the comparison noun.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: No como is required in this construction. Parece una nube means that something looks like a cloud; parecen nubes uses the plural verb and noun.

example.es: Desde lejos, las rocas parecen animales.
example.en: From far away, the rocks look like animals.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that an animal mates with another animal?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use aparearse con followed by the mate.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aparearse is pronominal, so its small pronoun changes with the subject. Con introduces the other animal.

example.es: Estas aves se aparean con parejas de la misma especie.
example.en: These birds mate with partners of the same species.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone resorts or turns to a measure?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use recurrir a followed by the measure, method, or person turned to.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of recurrir changes for the subject and time, but a remains before its complement.

example.es: El equipo recurrió a un plan alternativo.
example.en: The team resorted to an alternative plan.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happened a long time ago?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use hace mucho after the completed event.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mucho supplies an unspecified long amount of elapsed time. For an exact duration, Spanish can instead use hace dos años or another stated period.

example.es: Ese tren dejó de funcionar hace mucho.
example.en: That train stopped operating long ago.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name the final option used when other choices have failed?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Último comes before recurso because it ranks this option as the final one available.

example.es: La cirugía era el último recurso.
example.en: Surgery was the last resort.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say ‘in the eyes of’ or ‘from the perspective of’?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a ojos de before the person or group whose perspective is meant.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression is often figurative: a ojos del público means ‘in the public's eyes.’

example.es: A ojos de sus vecinos, era una heroína.
example.en: In the eyes of her neighbors, she was a heroine.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: orquídea · abeja extinta · pintura de una flor
cardDefinitions.answerEn: an orchid preserving a vanished bee's appearance as a living memory
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Some bee orchids evolved flowers that resemble female bees. The comic turns one self-pollinating orchid into a poignant memorial: even after the pollinating bee has disappeared, the flower's inherited shape still reflects how a plant once ‘saw’ that animal through evolution. Calling it a painting by a dying flower makes the biological relationship feel like art and remembrance.
